sections.markdown:
## C2 — Knowledge continuation and confusables: Changing lanes, traffic, passing and enforcement

FACT_ID: sec13-R01 | anchor: A46
When overtaking a bicycle going the same direction where the posted limit is 35 miles per hour or less, leave at least 3 feet between the vehicle’s rightmost projection and the bicycle’s left side. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R02 | anchor: A46
For the same-direction bicycle pass where the posted limit exceeds 35 miles per hour, the minimum separation is 6 feet. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R03 | anchor: A46
A motorist passing a same-direction bicycle may partly cross the centerline or a same-direction lane divider only when safe. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R04 | anchor: A46
Maintain the required bicycle-passing clearance until safely beyond the bicycle. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R05 | anchor: A46
Violating the quoted bicycle-overtaking Section 32-26-26.1 is a Class 2 misdemeanor. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R06 | anchor: A46
Acknowledge an officer’s enforcement stop by activating the right turn signal. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R07 | anchor: A46
Move to the right shoulder as guided by the patrol vehicle rather than the center median or the opposite side of a two-lane road. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R08 | anchor: A46
On a freeway, move fully onto the right shoulder even from an HOV lane and pull as far away from the travel roadway as possible. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R09 | anchor: A46
After dark during an enforcement stop, look for a well-lit stopping place such as near streetlights or services. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec13-R10 | anchor: A47
During an enforcement stop, end the phone conversation and switch off the radio to give the officer full attention. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-R11 | anchor: A47
Remain inside the vehicle unless the officer directs you to leave it. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-R12 | anchor: A47
Keep both the driver’s and passengers’ hands clearly visible during the stop. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec13-R13 | anchor: A47
If windows are tinted, the handbook recommends lowering them after stopping on the right shoulder and before the officer approaches to communicate. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0047]
